raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47868. In regular HTTP routing (`http-regular`), `Router::route_typed_request_once` created a `WorkerLoadGuard` only when the policy was `cache_aware` or `manual`. `power_of_two` compares `worker.load()`: it is the primary signal for `SGLANG_ROUTER_P2C_LOAD_METRIC=requests`/`least_requests` and the fallback for `tokens`. Without a guard that counter stayed at 0 on this route, so P2C selection there ignored in-flight requests. The PD router and the gRPC router already create the guard for every request.

## Modifications

- `sgl-model-gateway/src/routers/http/router.rs`: always create the `WorkerLoadGuard` for the selected worker, and make `send_typed_request` take it as `WorkerLoadGuard` instead of `Option`. The guard keeps its existing lifecycle: it is dropped after a non-streaming body is read, or attached to a streaming body with `AttachedBody`.
- `sgl-model-gateway/tests/routing/power_of_two_test.rs`: add `test_power_of_two_tracks_in_flight_requests`. It sends a `/generate` request to two slow mock workers under `power_of_two`, checks that the total worker load is 1 while the request is in flight, and checks that it returns to 0 afterwards.

`random` and `round_robin` now count load on this route too. This matches PD/gRPC routing and only costs an atomic increment and decrement per request.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: router-only change, model outputs unaffected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one atomic counter update per request.

## Testing

New test on base (`origin/main`) vs. with the fix:

```
# base
test routing::power_of_two_test::power_of_two_tests::test_power_of_two_tracks_in_flight_requests ... FAILED
assertion `left == right` failed: the selected worker should count the in-flight request
  left: 0
 right: 1

# with fix
test routing::power_of_two_test::power_of_two_tests::test_power_of_two_tracks_in_flight_requests ... ok
```

Full `cargo test --no-fail-fast --tests` in `sgl-model-gateway` (macOS, Rust 1.90):
- lib 397, api 86, inflight_tracker 11, load_guard_raii 6, mcp 20, metrics_aggregator 5, otel 10, reliability 57, security 47, spec 89, wasm 16: all pass.
- routing: 99 passed, 1 failed. The failing test is `test_openai_router_circuit_breaker`, which fails identically on base: it exercises the OpenAI router, which this PR does not touch, and depends on how the local resolver handles `http://invalid-url-that-will-fail`.
- Redis-backed tests were skipped because there is no local `redis-server`.

`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Developed with AI assistance.
